title: Private: add version compatibility policy + matrix for upgrade path gating
author: Quentin Harris
release_notes: Private upgrades now evaluate a compatibility policy before proceeding: unsupported version jumps are blocked; risky but supported paths emit warnings with remediation guidance.
description: Summary: Introduces a first-class compatibility policy for Redwood Private upgrades (VPC + on-prem) to deterministically block unsupported upgrade paths and warn on risky jumps. This is the policy layer consumed by the installer upgrade-plan generator and (in follow-ups) the control-plane / Console to provide consistent messaging. Motivation: We’ve had multiple upgrade-related incidents/near-misses driven by customers attempting multi-version jumps (or mixing control-plane/data-plane versions) without clear guardrails. This PR makes the supported upgrade surface area explicit and testable. Scope: - Adds a version compatibility matrix (source-of-truth) under `private/compat/compat-matrix.yaml` with explicit allowed transitions and constraints. - Adds a policy evaluator library (`private/compat`) that takes `current`, `target`, deployment mode (vpc|onprem), and optional Kubernetes/storage signals, then returns: `ALLOW`, `WARN`, or `BLOCK` with machine-readable reason codes and operator-facing messages. - Adds a CLI helper used by `redwood-private-installer` to render a stable summary (this is used by plan generation; the installer wiring lives in its repo). - Adds unit + golden tests for common paths and known failure cases (including SUP-18421 pattern: DB migration expectations when skipping intermediate minors). Compatibility semantics (v1): - Default supported path is N-1 -> N for Private platform versions (minor-to-minor or patch-to-patch), ALLOW. - N-2 -> N is WARN (supported for selected versions only; requires explicit operator acknowledgement in the installer). - Any cross-major jump is BLOCK unless explicitly whitelisted in the matrix. - Patch downgrades are BLOCK (rollback is handled by the upgrade state machine + artifacts; not by "downgrade to arbitrary patch"). - Control-plane and data-plane version skew: ALLOW within a bounded window defined in the matrix (currently: CP can be at N while DP at N-1 during staged rollouts; DP at N while CP at N-1 is BLOCK). - On-prem/air-gapped constraints: evaluator can return WARN when target version requires artifacts not present in the bundle manifest (reason code emitted; bundle verification lives elsewhere). Files/areas changed (high level): - `private/compat/compat-matrix.yaml`: initial matrix entries for 2025.04 -> 2025.05 and 2025.05 -> 2025.06; includes CP/DP skew bounds and notes. - `private/compat/evaluator.go`: semver-ish parser for Redwood Private version scheme + policy evaluation function. - `private/compat/reasons.go`: stable reason codes for auditability and support playbooks (e.g., `UNSUPPORTED_MAJOR_JUMP`, `DP_AHEAD_OF_CP`, `SKIP_TOO_MANY_MINORS`). - `private/compat/render.go`: canonical formatting for CLI/installer output (kept stable for docs and screenshots). - `private/compat/testdata/*`: golden test fixtures. - `docs/internal/private/compatibility.md`: internal notes for release engineering on updating the matrix per release train. Operator UX (as emitted by evaluator): - BLOCK example: "Upgrade blocked: current=2025.04.3 target=2025.06.0. Reason: unsupported upgrade jump (skips 2025.05). Remediation: upgrade to 2025.05.x first, verify health checks, then proceed to 2025.06.0." - WARN example: "Upgrade warning: N-2 -> N path allowed for this target but requires acknowledgement. Risks: longer DB migration time; ensure 2x storage headroom and maintenance window >= 60m." Checklist: - [x] Matrix is human-editable and code-reviewed - [x] Reason codes are stable and documented - [x] Unit tests cover allow/warn/block for common transitions - [x] Golden tests ensure CLI rendering stability - [x] Added "matrix freshness" CI check: fail if current release train target is missing from matrix (see notes in docs) Follow-ups (not in this PR): - Wire evaluator into installer prechecks + plan generation output (tracked in ENG-4821 / installer PR). - Emit evaluator outcomes to audit logs (planned in PR-29187). - Extend matrix with Kubernetes version constraints + storage backend notes once CI matrix is finalized (ENG-4877).

conversation: Ethan Park (review): Can we clarify where this policy is enforced today vs future? I’m concerned we’ll have matrix + library but no hard gate. Also: DP-ahead-of-CP rule should be BLOCK even if matrix would otherwise allow (safety). Quentin Harris (author): Added explicit notes in description + docs: enforcement in installer plan generation first; control-plane gating later. Also updated evaluator ordering so CP/DP skew checks run before matrix transition allowlist. Connor O'Brien (review): Matrix update workflow: who owns it and how do we prevent drift across release trains? Suggest a CI check that ensures the current release train has entries. Quentin Harris (author): Added `private-compat-matrix-check` workflow that validates matrix contains target versions listed in `release/PRIVATE_RELEASE_TRAIN` (simple text file). Also added docs section "Ownership" with Release Eng + Quentin as DRI and required reviewers. Sean Gallagher (review): WARN messaging should include concrete remediation requirements (maintenance window, storage headroom). We need consistent text so Support can copy/paste. Quentin Harris (author): Added renderer templates to keep messages consistent; included storage headroom + window suggestions in WARN output for skip paths. Naomi Feldman (security review): Ensure no sensitive environment details are included in rendered messages by default; reason codes are fine, but avoid leaking cluster names/URLs. Quentin Harris (author): Confirmed renderer only prints versions + reason codes; removed optional debug print of cluster identifier (was in an early commit). Rafael Mendes (SRE): For BLOCK: include explicit "do not proceed" language + link to runbook section, otherwise operators try to brute-force. Quentin Harris (author): Updated BLOCK template to include "Upgrade cannot proceed" and internal doc link placeholder used by installer docs. Approvals: Ethan Park approved after changes; Connor O'Brien approved; Sean Gallagher approved; Naomi Feldman approved with note to ensure audit log fields are handled in follow-up; Rafael Mendes approved. Merge: Squashed and merged to main.
